Read one layer of a vector file

Source: R/vector.R
read_layer.Rd

Reads one layer of a vector file or folder, such as a shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON or file geodatabase, as an sf data frame, with its attributes. It is the one way constechr reads vector files, so every tool reads them the same way and gets the same errors. Use it to read features with their attributes, such as polygons to summarise data by; use read_aoi() to read an area of interest.

Usage

read_layer(x, layer = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A single string: the path to a file or folder that GDAL can open as vector data, such as a shapefile (.shp), a folder of shapefiles, a GeoPackage (.gpkg), GeoJSON (.geojson) or a file geodatabase (.gdb).

layer

The layer to read: its name (a single string) or its position (a single whole number, from 1) in the list from sf::st_layers(). NULL (the default) reads the first layer, as sf::st_read() does; if x has more than one layer, a message names the layer read and lists the others.

...

Passed to sf::st_read(), such as query or wkt_filter. With query (an SQL query), the query selects what is read, and layer is only checked, not used. quiet = TRUE and stringsAsFactors = FALSE are the defaults; pass them to override.

Value

An sf data frame: one row per feature of the layer (none for an empty layer), with its attributes and geometry. A layer with no geometry column, such as a plain table, is an error. Nothing is written.

Method

  • Reading: sf::st_read() (GDAL) reads the layer chosen by layer: by name, by its position in sf::st_layers(), or the first layer when layer is NULL. With a query in ..., GDAL runs the query on x instead.

  • Nothing is transformed: the layer is returned as stored, with its CRS, Z and M coordinates, geometry types, attributes and geometry column name unchanged. Nothing is reprojected, validated, repaired or dissolved, and no areas or lengths are computed.

See also

read_aoi() to read an area of interest.

Examples

# The example GeoPackage, which has one layer, "aoi"
path <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")
sf::st_layers(path)
#> Driver: GPKG 
#> Available layers:
#>   layer_name geometry_type features fields               crs_name
#> 1        aoi       Polygon        1      1 Canada_Albers_WGS_1984

# The first layer (the default), by name or by position
read_layer(path)
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 1 field
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003600 ymin: 604300 xmax: 1005800 ymax: 606600
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>     name                           geom
#> 1 inside POLYGON ((1003600 606600, 1...
read_layer(path, layer = "aoi")
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 1 field
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003600 ymin: 604300 xmax: 1005800 ymax: 606600
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>     name                           geom
#> 1 inside POLYGON ((1003600 606600, 1...
read_layer(path, layer = 1)
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 1 field
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003600 ymin: 604300 xmax: 1005800 ymax: 606600
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>     name                           geom
#> 1 inside POLYGON ((1003600 606600, 1...

# Options for sf::st_read(), such as an SQL query
read_layer(path, query = "SELECT * FROM aoi WHERE name = 'inside'")
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 1 field
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003600 ymin: 604300 xmax: 1005800 ymax: 606600
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>     name                           geom
#> 1 inside POLYGON ((1003600 606600, 1...
